speaker: Doctor
text: I will begin by asking the mother about her pregnancy and delivery history, specifically looking for any infections or complications during labor. Can you describe the infant's feeding history and any changes in behavior since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and current neurological symptoms, I strongly suspect neonatal sepsis with meningitis. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the lumbar puncture and blood cultures are normal, we need to rule out other metabolic causes of seizures in this premature infant. What are the results of the serum glucose and electrolyte levels?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds. I also have Increasing lethargy over the past 18 hours, Appears ill.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Serum_Glucose REQUEST TEST: Serum_Calcium REQUEST TEST: Serum_Magnesium

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal metabolic and infectious workups, I am concerned about hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy given the low Apgar scores and prematurity. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Brain_MRI: Findings consistent with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy; EEG: Shows periodic high-voltage bursts with background suppression (burst-suppression pattern)

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and the characteristic burst-suppression pattern on EEG confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
